title: FFLAS prime right nullspace
objective: Generate and route a fast canonical Sage-compatible right-nullspace basis for dense GF(p), p < 256, through declared FFLAS/FFPACK packed FFI with FLINT capability fallback
references: SageMath dense GF(p) right kernel semantics

handoff.summary: Added one declared, generated, transactional packed-uint64 FFPACK right-nullspace boundary and a source-transparent typed-Python wrapper. The adapter retains no foreign pointer: it imports once, uses RAII to own FFPACK's allocated N-by-nullity column basis even across C++ exceptions, transposes to Sage's nullity-by-N row convention, canonicalizes only that smaller basis, exports once, and frees deterministically. Public dense GF(p) matrices select it for p < 256 beyond the measured 24-row/column crossover and retain declared FLINT for smaller inputs, larger primes, and unavailable hosts including native Windows. Random, structured, exhaustive binary, degenerate, rectangular, FLINT differential, SageMath 10.9 fixture, dynamic-adapter, isolated-native, and transactional-failure checks pass. On the 200x300 GF(97) workload, the generated boundary measured 1.58 ms, the current FLINT shim 9.57 ms, and public Matrix 2.39 ms.
risks: FFLAS/FFPACK remains an optional Unix dependency; native Windows deliberately follows the already-tested declared FLINT fallback.
The crossover was measured on Linux x64 with one OpenBLAS thread. The conservative threshold keeps tiny matrices on FLINT, but future platform-specific tuning may improve it.

FFPACK NullSpaceBasis allocates its result. The local RAII owner is established before the call and receives the output pointer by reference so stack unwinding frees even an allocation published before a later C++ exception.
next_steps: Integrate both commits onto dense-qq-resources and rerun the broad native suite from the primary worktree where the M4RI artifact is provisioned.

Consider a generated result-shape protocol later to allocate only nullity-by-columns output; the current columns-squared buffer matches the existing FLINT ABI and costs under one millisecond at the measured size.
